messages.subject: Lavaan Warning Message
parts:
Hi all,

I have been using Lavaan for about a year now, after switching from MPlus... (new computer, didn't feel like buying a new subscription)  

Anyway, I have not had any trouble until recently when I updated to R 3.0.0 and the most recent lavaan package.

I have been running the script:

model2 <-'
  PerceivedAddiction =~ CPUI_Comp + CPUI_Efforts + K_SCS

  Moral_Attitudes ~ Religiosity
  PerceivedAddiction ~ Religiosity + Moral_Attitudes + 
  Neuroticism + Self_Control

  CPUI_Comp ~~ CPUI_Efforts
  CPUI_Comp ~~ K_SCS
  CPUI_Efforts ~~ K_SCS
'
fit <- sem(model2, data = Moral_Transgressions)
summary(fit, fit.measures=TRUE)

and I get the following message each time:
> model2 <-'
+   PerceivedAddiction =~ CPUI_Comp + CPUI_Efforts + K_SCS
+ 
+   Moral_Attitudes ~ Religiosity
+   PerceivedAddiction ~ Religiosity + Moral_Attitudes + Neuroticism + Self_Control
+ '
> fit <- sem(model2, data = Moral_Transgressions)

--Error in `[.data.frame`(data, , unlist(ov.names)) : 
  undefined columns selected
> summary(fit, fit.measures=TRUE)---

Any thoughts on what is leading to that error message?  My data is good, and will run through other programs and R packages (OpenMX works, but I don't like it).  Also, when I try to re-run old models that I had previously established, I get a very similar message.  

Any pointers would be great.  

Thanks!

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Lavaan Warning Message
parts:
On 04/05/2013 06:13 PM, Joshua Grubbs wrote:

> > fit <- sem(model2, data = Moral_Transgressions)
>
> --Error in `[.data.frame`(data, , unlist(ov.names)) :
> undefined columns selected

Perhaps your new computer has a new locale? What do you get if you type in:

names(Moral_Transgressions)

and then

lavaanNames(lavaanify(model2))

The error message is saying there some mismatch between the two...

Yves.

messages.author: 2404607b7e3e8987
messages.subject: Re: Lavaan Warning Message
parts:
Thanks so much for the reply.  

The [names(Moral_Transgressions) ] command returned the variables from my dataset; and the  [lavaanNames(lavaanify(model2)) ] command returend all of the variables from my model... and the two matched perfectly.  

However, when I run the model again, it still gives me:

> fit <- sem(model2, data=Moral_Transgressions)

I deleted all of the data-sets that I had, re-created my data set from the original, and reran the analyses, and it worked.  I am now assuming that something was corrupt in my dataset.  

Thank you so much for your reply.  Your accessibility as a developer makes using this package much easier!
